## Goal
ROADMAP 3.1 puts the Spanish UI in 0.5. The inventories so far cover the wizard (WO-250, WO-254), the CLI (WO-232) and letters and exposure messages (WO-290). Nothing lists the user-facing sentences that the delivery engine builds in code: the run summary (`engine/runner.py:104-130`), the "needs you" notification body (`runner.py:985`) and the hand-off help text `GENERIC_HELP` (`engine/handoff.py:69`), the complaint to-do title and body (`runner.py:957-970`), the listing finder banners `MSG_*` (`engine/listing_finder.py:78-93`), the fill-for-me banners `MSG_*` (`engine/fill_for_me.py:68-74`), the monthly update (`notify.py:78-84`) and the assisted to-do steps (`submitters/assisted.py:55-78`). Inventory them (docs only) in a new file with the facts a translator needs, so no one has to read Python.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. One table per source file: id (file + constant or function), the English text exactly as in code, file:line, where it is shown (toast, dashboard card, terminal, banner in a broker page), and who reads it (Pat, a helper, a developer).
2. For every sentence built from pieces (f-strings, counts with singular/plural, a person's label inserted, a state word inserted such as `k.value.replace('_', ' ')` at `runner.py:112-114`), a "needs care" note: word order, plural rules (Spanish has no "(s)" trick like "site(s)"), gender agreement, and what the placeholder holds.
3. A list of strings that are developer-only (log lines, exception text) and are NOT to be translated, with file:line, so the translator knows to skip them.
4. A "do not translate" list for fixed tokens (state codes like `needs_human`, flags, file names).
5. Counts at the top: how many user-facing strings, how many with placeholders, how many with plural logic.
6. Every file:line citation resolves on main (check each when you finish); the document says "line numbers from main on <date>".
7. Plain words, no promises, no "guarantee/erase/100%"; fake people only in examples.

Docs/tests-only work in Codex's lane. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL), offline, Windows-safe paths. Check `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard. Every claim cites file:line from main at the time of writing; re-check them.
